_comment: The one hand written file in this directory. derive_names.py writes one
<prefix>.json per namespace and never touches this one; the fork's
<ClassNames> option merges every *.json of the directory, and a scoped
key cannot collide with the derived unscoped key it refines.
These are the classes the generator invents for w:t, w:instrText and
w:delInstrText inside w:r: all three have the type CT_Text, so a compound
field needs one class per element name to tell them apart, and there is no
docx4j name to take because JAXB used one Text class with a JAXBElement
per name. Left alone they come out T2, InstrText2 and DelInstrText2, and
w:t is the most used element in the model. They are named here the way the
generator already names the sibling classes of the same field, R.Cr as RCr
and R.Tab as RTab, which is how docx4j names them too: R.T is RT. Each is
a subclass of Text, so isinstance(x, Text) holds, as CR-001 section 11
question 2 requires.
The scope is the enclosing class as the generator holds it when it invents
the class, which is the schema type name (CT_P) unless the type is used by
exactly one global element and has been reduced into it, which is the case
here: CT_R is w:r. It is read in this file's namespace, so it is wml's w:r
and not OMML's CT_R, which also carries a w:t.
CT_StylePaneFilter is the second hand entry (CR-002 section 5.7): the type
does not exist in docx4j's schema copy at all --- the schema patch in
schemas/wml/wml.xsd adds it --- so derive_names.py has no docx4j name to
give it and xsdata would call it CtStylePaneFilter. Named here the way
docx4j names every CT_ type it did not rename, CTShortHexNumber and
CTSignedTwipsMeasure being its neighbours.
